verdict: This is a genuinely well-engineered project for its stage: the append-only event log with pure projections, the capability-shaped clone-to-RCE boundary, and the write-time cost pricing with NULL-means-unpriced discipline are all better than most shipping agent CLIs. But the project's own brand — 'measured, not assumed' — is currently undercut by its docs: the README/ROADMAP assert a green 575-test suite while the measured run shows 1 failed + 24 skipped, the README/ROADMAP claim a PHAR distribution that DECISIONS.md §8–9 explicitly decided against ('no PHAR'), and the TUI capture shipped as the hero image still shows the billed-'exit' bug and a spacing-mangled hint line. The single biggest improvement is a docs-vs-reality reconciliation pass enforced by CI, because right now the project's most distinctive asset — its honesty — has drifted.
strengths: CostLedger's 'NULL cost means unpriced, never $0.00' discipline, enforced by golden tests in both directions (CostTableTest/CostJsonGoldenTest), is exemplary accounting design.

The clone-to-RCE boundary is capability-shaped and layered (ProjectEnv::fromEnvironment, SkillLibrary, LibraryIndex::refusesPath, McpClient::configPath) with refusal notices that are announced, never silent.
EventLog's seq-allocation story (transaction-bounded allocation, driver-aware migration, documented concurrency reproduction) is exactly how load-bearing ordering should be handled.

findings.title: Fix the failing test and reconcile every '575 passing' claim with the real suite result
findings.reason: The measured suite is 'Tests: 1 failed, 24 skipped, 576 passed (3384 assertions)', yet the README badge says 'tests-575 passing', the status table says '✅ 575 passing, 3381 assertions', and ROADMAP.md §1 repeats '✅ 575 passing'. For a project whose erratum section scolds an autonomous run because 'the run's scoring loop graded polish, not the release gate', shipping a README that asserts a green suite while a red test exists is the same failure mode one layer up.
findings.suggestion: Make the test-count badge generated, not typed: a CI step runs the hermetic suite, writes the count to a JSON artifact, and a badge/check fails on any non-zero failure count. Until then, fix or xfail the one failing test and update README/ROADMAP to '576 passed, 1 failed, 24 skipped' with the failing test named.
findings.evidence: README: '[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-575%20passing-brightgreen...)]' vs measured 'Tests: 1 failed, 24 skipped, 576 passed (3384 assertions)'

findings.title: Resolve the PHAR contradiction between DECISIONS.md and README/ROADMAP
findings.reason: DECISIONS.md §8 states the distribution decision as 'Composer package + FrankenPHP embed binary, no PHAR, no Docker-as-distribution' and §9 restates it 'CONFIRMED on both axes'. Yet the README status table says '📦 curl | sh installer ✅ live — PHAR built 32MB (build/paider.phar via box, 222ms), FrankenPHP trimmed still deferred' and ROADMAP.md §1 says 'Distribution | ✅ PHAR 32MB, curl | sh live'. These cannot all be true: either the no-PHAR decision was reversed (and DECISIONS.md needs a §23 recording it) or the README is describing an artifact the decision log says should not exist.
findings.suggestion: Add a DECISIONS.md entry that explicitly supersedes §8/§9's 'no PHAR' clause if the PHAR is now the shipped distribution path, and update §8/§9 with a 'superseded by §N' pointer — the same convention the file already uses for its own superseded measurements. Then make README and ROADMAP cite that entry.
findings.evidence: DECISIONS.md §8: 'no PHAR, no Docker-as-distribution is now CONFIRMED on both axes' vs README: 'PHAR built 32MB (build/paider.phar via box, 222ms)'

findings.title: Scrub secrets from tool_call event payloads, not just conversation messages
findings.reason: Loop::remember() routes all user/assistant content through ProseStream::scrubSecrets() before it reaches the log ('session->pushHistory($role, ProseStream::scrubSecrets($content))'), but the tool_call event is appended raw: " $this->eventLog->append('tool_call', ['tool' => $call['name'], 'input' => $call['input'], 'ok' => $result->ok]) ". A run_shell command like 'curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..."' — exactly the kind of thing a coding agent is asked to do — lands verbatim in the plaintext .paider/paider.db, which STORAGE.md describes as 'local-only' but which is also the corpus RagStore embeds and sends to PAIDER_EMBEDDING_URL.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same ProseStream::scrubSecrets() to the serialized tool input (per string value in $call['input'], recursively) before the append('tool_call', ...) in Loop::turn, and add a test asserting a keyed shell command never appears in the event payload.
findings.evidence: Loop::turn: "$this->eventLog->append('tool_call', ['tool' => $call['name'], 'input' => $call['input'], 'ok' => $result->ok]);" — no scrubSecrets, vs remember(): 'ProseStream::scrubSecrets($content)' on every message

findings.title: Stop LibraryIndex::refusesPath from refusing the operator's own ~/.paider/skills
findings.reason: refusesPath()'s docblock says 'Everything else — a path the user names explicitly, outside a project, in their own home — is allowed, because the user pointing at it IS the authorisation.' But the depth-tail check ('Any path with the shape of a project-local agent config (.paider/… or .claude/…) is refused anywhere on the filesystem') matches the user's own trusted home directory too: for '/home/me/.paider/skills', the last two segments are '.paider/skills', so fromPath('/home/me/.paider/skills', ...) returns refused — the exact directory STORAGE.md and SkillLibrary designate as 'the ONLY place skills are discovered from' and 'user-owned and user-trusted'.
findings.suggestion: Exempt the resolved home path before the shape check: compute $home = realpath(getenv('HOME').'/.paider') and, if $real is inside it, return false (the user naming their own home library is the stated authorisation). Add a test: LibraryIndex::refusesPath(getenv('HOME').'/.paider/skills') === false while refusesPath('/tmp/clone/.paider/skills') === true.
findings.evidence: refusesPath(): '$tail = implode(DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR, array_slice($segments, -$depth)); if ($tail === $wanted ...) return true;' — matches /home/<user>/.paider/skills, contradicting the docblock's 'a path the user names explicitly, outside a project, in their own home — is allowed'

findings.title: Fix the TUI's collapsed hint text and regenerate the hero capture, which still shows the billed-exit bug
findings.reason: The screenshot shows the quit hint rendering as 'type/quitto exit' — the spaces around '/quit' live inside adjacent Termwind spans ('type /quit (or exit) to quit' in ChatCommand::handle) and are being collapsed in the rendered box, making the single most-shown line of the UI read as one token. The same capture shows the model line truncated mid-token ('anthropic/claude-opus-'), and — most damning for a README that just spent a paragraph explaining why a corrupt hero image 'makes people draw false conclusions about the code' — it shows 'exit' sitting in the input box with a spinner already running, i.e. the exact billed-exit behaviour commits b05edbe/656f6f9 claim is fixed.
findings.suggestion: Render the hint as a single span with inline colour via Palette::wrap instead of three sibling div spans so whitespace survives; widen or wrap the spinner model label (PhpSpinner) so it never truncates mid-model-id; and re-run bin/capture-tui.sh post-fix so the README hero shows the current behaviour, matching the standard the README itself sets for capture artifacts.
findings.evidence: Screenshot: 'type/quitto exit' (collapsed spaces), spinner line 'anthropic/claude-opus-' (truncated), and 'exit' in the input box with spinner running; ChatCommand renders 'type /quit (or exit) to quit'
